entities.summary:
The Battle of Kolín was a pivotal event in the Third Silesian War, fought on June 18, 1757, in what is now the Czech Republic. This decisive battle saw the Austrian forces, led by Maximilian Ulysses Count Browne, clash with the Prussian army, commanded by Frederick the Great. The outcome was a crushing defeat for the Prussians, who suffered heavy losses and were forced to retreat.

The Battle of Kolín had significant consequences for the region, leading to the eventual partition of Silesia and shaping the balance of power in Central Europe. The battle also showcased the military prowess of Frederick the Great, who would go on to become one of the most celebrated military leaders in history.

The legacy of the Battle of Kolín can be seen in the subsequent wars and alliances that formed in the region, as well as the impact it had on the development of military tactics and strategy. The battle remains an important chapter in the history of the region and a testament to the bravery and skill of the soldiers who fought there.

As Frederick the Great himself noted, 'The Battle of Kolín was a victory of genius over brute force, and it will always be remembered as a shining example of the power of intellect and strategy in warfare.'
